ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Using the food web diagram, what would happen to the amount of turtle grass if the green sea turtle population were reduced?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: There would be more turtle grass
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram. In the lower left of the diagram is labeled “Turtle Grass,” and above it is labeled “Green Sea Turtle.” There is an arrow from “Turtle Grass” pointing to “Green Sea Turtle,” indicating that energy or food flows from turtle grass to the green sea turtle. Reasoning: In a food web, arrows usually indicate the organism being eaten pointing to the consumer, so the green sea turtle eats turtle grass. If the number of green sea turtles decreases, then the turtle grass eaten by the green sea turtles will decrease, so the amount of turtle grass will increase.
